question: A 27-year-old woman goes to the genetic counseling clinic after having a child with Down syndrome. In the child, a trisomy 21 with translocation 21/21 inherited from the mother is identified. What would be the risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in the future children of this woman?

options.opa: The risk of recurrence will be 10-15%, as in the rest of translocations.
options.opb: 100% of viable fetuses will be born with Down syndrome.
options.opc: The risk of recurrence will be very low (12%).
options.opd: The risk of recurrence will be 50%.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Translocation 21/21 in the child -> Inherited from the mother -> Mother is a carrier of the translocation -> Risk of recurrence in future children is increased -> Risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in future children is higher than the general population -> Unclear if the risk is -> 100%
enhanced_information: The risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in future children of this woman is not 100%. The presence of translocation 21/21 in the child inherited from the mother does increase the risk, but it is not an absolute certainty. The actual risk may be higher than the general population but is not specified as 100%.
analysis: The core medical principle is that the risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in future children of a mother with a translocation 21/21 is increased but not 100%. While the risk is higher than the general population, it is not an absolute certainty. The actual risk may vary but is not specified as 100%.
